messages:
mina: Heads-up — planning a minimal chroot/pivot-root runtime canary for the base-image rebuild next week. Need quick sign-off on RBAC for the signing agent, audit logging paths, and KMS access. Who can pick pieces up?

sam: I can take RBAC. Clarify: are we reusing the existing image-signer service account or creating an ephemeral one for the canary?

mina: Prefer ephemeral: `image-builder-canary@` pattern. Short-lived creds, scoped roles (only staging). Needs KMS sign/verify and write to the audit bucket. Also want runtime to drop auxv and remove suid bits from binaries.

olivia: Agreed on suid removal. Quick Dockerfile snippet for runtime we discussed:```dockerfile
FROM scratch
COPY --from=builder /app /app
RUN find / -perm /6000 -type f -exec chmod a-s {} + || true
USER 65532
ENTRYPOINT ["/app/launcher"]
```
Keep image minimal and strip /proc/sysrq and unneeded syscalls via seccomp.

jacob: On KMS & IAM: give the ephemeral signer SA only `roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier` for the cosign key in staging. Grant `roles/storage.objectCreator` to the signer for `gs://redwood-image-audit/staging/*` only via IAM condition. I'll draft the IAM binding with condition on resource name and project tag.

sec-oncall: For audit logging — ensure builder sets structured fields: `build_id`, `canary: true`, `signer: image-builder-canary`. Export builder logs to a dedicated log sink -> BigQuery/SIEM with 90d retention. Also runtime should forward kernel/auditd events to SIEM; add rule to alert on execve of unexpected binaries.

tara: Canary rollout proposal: deploy `minimal-chroot-v1` to 10% of staging pods for 48h with synthetic health checks (latency, jwt validation, syscall error rates). Fallback: update deployment image/tag back to previous signed image and pin. Question: if we discover a signing key compromise, can we revoke signatures?

sam: Short answer: KMS key disable stops future signs but does not invalidate existing signatures. Our rollback should rely on image routing / tag pinning and removing the new tag from registries if needed. Add attestation policy in deployment pipeline to prefer keys with creation_time < X if needed.

build-bot: build started (simulated): `buildctl build --frontend=dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=./`
[build-bot] LOG: cosign sign --key projects/staging/locations/global/keyRings/canary/cryptoKeys/signer
[build-bot] LOG: pushed image gcr.io/redwood/staging/minimal-chroot:v1-canary

mina: Action items: @sam — update IAM doc with ephemeral SA and conditional bindings; @jacob — schedule cosign KMS key creation for staging and add IAM snippet; @olivia — PR Dockerfile changes + seccomp profile; @tara — draft canary runbook with rollback steps; @sec-oncall — add SIEM mappings and alert for `canary:true` execve spikes. I'll set a 30m sync Tue 10am PT. :calendar:

sec-oncall: Ack. I'll add an alert: if syscall anomalies > 3x baseline for canary tag within 15m, page sec-oncall and eng-oncall. Also will add audit field mappings for easy queries.

mina: Thanks all — let's keep the canary tight and timeboxed. I'll post the PR links in this thread when available. :thumbsup:
